title: VICTORIA - Validation of Innovative Cancer care with Trodelvy® for Outcomes in Real World Data in Inoperable and/or Advanced HER2-negative breast cancer patients
summary:
Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women worldwide. Certain subtypes, such as triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer, are particularly difficult to treat. When breast cancer cannot be removed by surgery (is unresectable) or has spread to other organs (metastatic disease), it is usually not curable. Treatment then aims to prolong survival and maintain quality of life.

Sacituzumab govitecan is a newer anti-cancer medicine that has shown improved survival in clinical trials for patients with unresectable or metastatic breast cancer. Clinical studies also suggest that quality of life may be maintained or improved during treatment. However, limited information is available on how this treatment performs in routine clinical practice in Germany.

This non-interventional study aims to collect real-world data on overall survival, disease progression, and quality of life in patients with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (aTNBC) or hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (HR+/HER2- aBC) receiving sacituzumab govitecan in routine care. The study will also describe how the treatment is managed in everyday practice, including treatment duration, dose adjustments, discontinuations, and management of side effects.

The study will be conducted prospectively in up to 20 oncology centers and practices across Germany. No additional study-specific medical procedures will be performed. Treatment decisions are made solely by the treating physician according to routine clinical practice. Patients will be followed for up to 24 months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Male or female patients aged 18 years or older at baseline (before SG initiation)
2.	Patients with an unresectable and/or metastatic BC
3.	Patients with available information on HR and HER2 status of BC and a confirmed aTNBC or HR+/HER2- aBC
4.	Patients who are initiating SG therapy, according to tumor board decision prior to start of SG therapy at one of the participating study sites and the manufacturer’s labeling as below
o	unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (mTNBC) who have received two or more prior systemic therapies, at least one of them for metastatic disease or unresectable locally advanced or 
o	metastatic hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative (IHC 0, IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH–) breast cancer who have received endocrine-based therapy and at least two additional systemic therapies in the metastatic setting
5.	Patients who sign the informed consent form (ICF) indicate that they understand the purpose of the study and its required procedures and are willing to participate in it
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Patients with known hypersensitivity to SG or to any of the drug’s excipients
2.	Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding at enrollment date
3.	Patients enrolled in a clinical trial at enrollment date (patients enrolled in a non-interventional trial are not excluded)
4.	Patients who had SG treatment prior to enrollment date
